domain: hydrological risk operations - river-station alert-threshold exceedance prediction (Colombia, IDEAM automatic-station telemetry)
prediction_question: HYPOTHESIS under test: given a Colombian river station's hourly maximum-level telemetry through hour H (raw automatic-sensor readings, published openly on datos.gov.co), predict whether the water level will exceed the station's official alert threshold within the next 48 hours. A useful prediction feeds municipal early-warning (IDEAM/Carabineros/SNGRD protocols) with lead time for evacuation and road closures. The exact missing fact: an official per-station alert/danger threshold in machine-readable form - without it the label degrades to a self-referential percentile, which is a different (weaker) task.
prediction_time: Telemetry is hourly and near-real-time on the live feed; the published dataset is one current table of raw unvalidated sensor values (publisher clause: 'los datos ... no han sido validados por el IDEAM'), and IDEAM documents a preliminary -> en revision -> definitivo lifecycle for its validated series (separate 'Niveles Horarios' dataset). UNRESOLVED: the as-of policy - current raw values may later be corrected, so features computed from today's table may differ from what the live feed showed at the time; construction must either use only the raw-feed table (accepting and measuring the revision effect) or obtain vintage information. This is the main open question besides the threshold.
target_definition: PROPOSED (blocked on threshold source): binary - station-hour (or station-day) level exceedance of the official alert threshold within (H, H+48]. Label source: valorobservado hourly maxima (cm/m) per station; the threshold would come from an official IDEAM table (NOT FOUND in the bounded probe: the station catalog cqmv-a99d has no threshold columns, and a catalog search for alert-level datasets returned nothing machine-readable). Fallback (weaker): per-station seasonal high-quantile exceedance - requires a known-event fixture (e.g. a documented 2021-2025 flood on a specific river) before that route may be probed further.

measurements.probe_2026_10_23: Socrata metadata + SoQL (scripts in session scratch): rows 14,672,316; span 2001-01-01..2026-10-21; 345 stations; rows-by-year listed in sources; sample rows show hourly 'Nivel Maximo' in metres with station/department/municipio/zona metadata; catalog has no threshold columns; catalog v1 search for alert-threshold datasets returned no machine-readable result.
measurements.capacity_note: Volume ample (26 years, 14.7M rows, 345 stations). Positives are now MEASURED on the demonstration station (El Banco: both classes in all three candidate windows, day-level rates 7.7%/16.6%/11.6%) but NOT at panel scale: the IHD threshold harvest, per-station frame validation and clustered-count measurement are the remaining measurements before split windows can be fixed.
measurements.threshold_hunt_2026_10_23_pass2: RESOLVED: official per-station flood thresholds (cotas) exist and are extractable. Current BAH/ITD/BCH bulletins (Oct 2026, fetched, 3 files text-extracted) carry zone-level alerts only; the per-station 'COTA CRITICA x.xx m' values live in the historical IHD (Informe Hidrologico) PDFs, Wayback-archived (CDX captures 2017-2025) - 16 station values extracted from one Oct-2024 IHD (pypdf, regex recipe in notes), with decade-stability evidence (Puerto Salgar 6.20 / El Banco 8.30 identical in 2014 and 2024 bulletins). No machine-readable threshold dataset exists on datos.gov.co; h4gs-wsmg Alertas Hidrologicas is a non-tabular view (403 row/column access). Join evidence: 345 distinct telemetry stations; telemetry names carry 2-3 spelling variants per code; name-only joins produce false pairs (PUERTO ANGOSTURAS/Ariari vs ANGOSTURA/Magdalena measured) - join must use codigoestacion + river + municipio. Measured exceedances (SoQL): EL BANCO 0025027020 cota 8.30 -> 5,937/105,354 hourly obs 2015-2026 (5.64%); distinct days over cota: train 2015-2019 137/1,777 days-with-data, eval 2020-2023 137/828, holdout 2024-2026 111/957 - both classes in all three windows on this station, positives clustered into flood episodes, telemetry gaps measured (eval window has data on 828 of ~1,461 days). CABUYARO 0035107030 cota 7.36 -> telemetry from 2026-03-28 only. MITU 0042077020 cota 10.20 -> 0/29,688 obs - unexplained frame/station anomaly; every joined station needs the zero/always-positive sanity check before entering the panel.

review: The one blocking fact from the first pass (does an official threshold exist in any obtainable form?) is resolved YES: IDEAM publishes per-station cotas in IHD chart annotations, archived harvestably, with decade-stable values; one station (El Banco) already measures both classes across all three candidate windows. The task is now an engineering-scale-up question (harvest + join + per-station validation), not an existence question. Measured false-pair and frame anomalies (ANGOSTURA collision, MITU zero positives) are recorded as construction hazards, not reasons to drop.
next_action: Threshold blocker RESOLVED (official cotas extractable from Wayback-archived IHD PDFs; recipe + 16-value demonstration in notes s5-6). Remaining, in order: (1) IHD harvest: sweep Wayback CDX for IHD PDFs 2016-2024 (patterns recorded in notes), extract the full station-cota table, dedupe by station with value-change log; (2) join to telemetry by codigoestacion with river/municipio confirmation (name-only joins measured to produce false pairs - ANGOSTURA case in notes); exclude or explain zero/always-positive anomalies per station (MITU case); (3) per-station continuity (gap rates) + day-level exceedance base rates on the joined set over candidate windows; record clustered (episode) counts, not just day counts; (4) raw-vs-validated as-of comparison (vfth-yucv vs ig79-2jr9 for a fixed station-month) and the current-vintage policy statement; (5) novelty check (check-novelty.py) before any ready verdict. Then re-verdict: ready only if the joined panel carries enough valid stations with both classes per window.
